name: Parse Server
tagline: Open source Firebase alternative. Node.js backend, MongoDB or Postgres.
shortDescription: The original open source BaaS, originally by Facebook. Now community-maintained. Node.js server with MongoDB/Postgres, auth, file storage, GraphQL, and push notifications.
longDescription:
## What it is

Parse Server is the open source backend that Facebook open-sourced in 2016 after shutting down its hosted Parse service. Node.js server with MongoDB or Postgres, REST + GraphQL APIs, auth (email, OAuth, MFA), file storage (S3-compatible), push notifications, and cloud code jobs.

## Why we recommend it

If you were on the original Parse and migrated away, you can come back. If you need a self-hostable BaaS with the same primitives as Firebase (auth, DB, storage, push), Parse Server is the most mature option.

## When to use it

- Migration target from legacy Parse apps
- Self-hosted BaaS for mobile apps
- Node.js apps that need auth + DB + push without writing boilerplate
- IoT backends with millions of devices
installInstructions:
**Docker:**
```
docker run -d --name parse -p 1337:1337 parseplatform/parse-server --appId APP_ID --masterKey MASTER_KEY --databaseURI mongodb://mongo:27017/parse
```

**MongoDB or Postgres:** Set `--databaseURI` accordingly.
pricingDetails: Free. Open source under BSD-3. Self-host on your own infra. Back4app, SashiDo offer managed Parse.
